preview: Interview experience at MSCI covering online assessment, technical rounds, DSA, LLD, and HR discussion resulting in a full-time offer.
content: Abhishek Kalshetti B.Tech CE 2018-2022 Morgan Stanley Capital International FTE Eligibility: CGPA 6.75 and above Branches Allowed: CS, IT, EXTC Timeline and Events: August 4: Pre-Placement Talk It was a 1hr presentation in which they talked about the firm, tech stacks, work culture, what values they are looking for, etc. (Do pay attention to important slides like tech stacks, core values, work culture, cause you can leverage your resume/experiences to be a good fit in the firm) Online Assessment: The test was conducted on Hacker-rank. Time: 60 Mins Total Questions: 17 MCQ’s: 16 (SQL Queries, OS, OOPS, DSA) Coding: A variation of Edit Distance (Dynamic Programming) https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/edit-distance-dp-5/ Selected Candidates received Mails on the same day for Round 2 Interviews, scheduled for the next day. A total of 39 students were shortlisted for Round 2 Round 2 (Technical): My Interview was Scheduled for 5 PM on 5th August. Platform: Microsoft Teams In this round, my DSA Skills were tested. Questions: 1.Introduce yourself. Keep this short and simple. Mention your internship in a line or two. Techstacks you’ve worked on, similarly mention your projects in a line or two. (Tip: Your introduction should sound very confident i.e your first impression is what will set the tone for further interview) 2.How to find a loop in a linked list. Explain your approach first don’t jump into coding directly, run the question again with the interviewer, give a test case and confirm that your answer is correct. As it was a virtual interview, I had the option to share my screen and draw diagrams/approaches on paint. Explain your approach then code on note pad/text editor. 2.a Find the start point of the loop 2.b Length of Loop 2.c Difference between LinkedList and Array 3.Find the first repeated character in a string https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/find-the-first-repeated-character-in-a-string/ I used a unorder_map for this question, so the interviewer asked me how unorder_map is implemented in C++. So, again I drew the implementation on paint and wrote Sudo code on notepad. 4.Minimum swap required to convert binary tree to binary search tree. First, explained my approach. Explained how I am going to store the inorder traversal (i.e I’ll store the nodes in a vector) Tip: (Always explain your code while writing it. Don’t wait to complete your code and then explain because the interviewer won’t understand what you are doing and most importantly there will be a huge pause which you need to avoid. Keep the interview engaging interviewer may even give you hints use them and complete your code.) I completed the code and did a dry run on a given test case. The interviewer was satisfied with my approach. 5.Given a sequence of words, print all anagrams together. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/given-a-sequence-of-words-print-all-anagram s-together/ First, I gave a brute force solution. The interviewer asked me for an optimized approach. Was able to do it with the implementation of HashMap. 6.Interviewer asked me if I had questions. I asked what tech stack they are working on, work culture in MSCI. This round lasted for 1hr. Round 3 (Techincal + HR) This round lasted for 1hr and all the questions I was asked were of DSA, Puzzles, LLD. 1.Return the longest path from the root to a leaf node. Used a recursive approach.Did a dry run to explain function calls. The interviewer was satisfied with my approach. 2.Design a movie ticket booking system like Bookmyshow https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/design-movie-ticket-booking-system-like-boo kmyshow/ (A lot of discussions was done on this try to apply concepts like inheritance, abstract classes, etc to increase code reusability) 3.Egg Dropping Question First, the interviewer asked me it in a puzzle form, for example, I have 100 eggs and 100 floors and I have to minimize the attempts to get to know the floor at which eggs start to break and what if now I have 2 eggs and 100 floors, how will my approach change. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/egg-dropping-puzzle-dp-11/ Then the interviewer asked me to code the solution. I first used a recursive approach, the interviewer asked if I can optimize the solution. I did a dry run on recursive code and found overlapping sub-problems, applied memoization on the recursive solution. The interviewer was quite happy with my approach. 4.Asked questions on my internship. 5.Asked some questions on API’s, Flutter (since I mentioned mobile application project in my resume) 6.What is the domain in which you are most confident. I said that I am very confident about my mobile application development skills but at the same time I don’t want to label myself that I want to work in a particular domain. 7.Had a brief discussion on how financial markets are affected due to covid and how can things change with time. My round ended around 5 PM. Results were announced at 7.30 PM,6 out of 23 were selected and I am happy to share that I was one of them. Followed by HR discussions at 8 PM. Tips: 1.Be calm, interviewers are generally helpful, keep explaining your approach step by step if you get stuck interviewer will give you hints use them, and complete your code. 2.You have to present your ideas/approaches very clearly. The interviewer must know what are you trying to do at each point. 3.You should know each and everything mentioned in your resume. That is you should be able to defend everything asked about your internships and projects. Resources: 1.GFG Must do coding questions https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/must-do-coding-questions-for-companies-like-amazon-m icrosoft-adobe/ 2.Dynamic Programming https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nqowUJzG-iM&list=PL_z_8CaSLPWekqhdCPmFoh ncHwz8TY2Go 3.Graphs https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YTtpfjGlH2M&list=PLgUwDviBIf0rGEWe64KWas0Nr yn7SCRWw 4.Puzzles https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzles/ All the Best!!
